pathway.title: Block, Inc. — Full credit assessment
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: Liquidity is the strongest support and does most of the work: cash and cash equivalents cover the 2027 convertible notes 13.67x, issuer-stated total liquidity covers the notes principal 1.74x, the USD 900 million revolver is undrawn, no senior note falls due before 2030, and 90.04% of the notes principal falls due in four series from 2030 to 2033. Part of the cash is deposit-funded and customer-related float is large, so the cushion is real but not all of it is the issuer's own money. Basis: calculation CASHCOV-20260930; calculation LIQCOV-20260930; calculation WALL-2030-2033; Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_xyz-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 4, 27–28, 55–56

Leverage is measure-dependent, so no single ratio settles the credit: total debt is 4.64x reported EBITDA and 1.68x adjusted EBITDA, notes alone are 3.65x and 1.32x, and interest cover is 3.99x reported against 11.03x adjusted. The add-backs are 63.87% of adjusted EBITDA and include the contingency and restructuring charges that are partly cash, so the reported figures are the safer guide until the regulatory matter is settled. Basis: calculation NOTESLEV-20260930; calculation ADDBACK-LTM; Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_xyz-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 53–54

Cash flow is strong but not clean: operating cash flow in nine months of 2026 was 53.24% higher than a year earlier and purchases of property and equipment were only 4.26% of it, leaving a proxy of USD 2,873,585 thousand, yet the figure includes movements in loans and customer balances and an unexplained inflow in other assets and liabilities. Light capital intensity gives flexibility, but conversion of earnings to free cash is not established. Basis: calculation FCFPROXY-9M2026; Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_xyz-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 7–8

Retained consumer lending is the main credit-quality exposure: loans held for investment grew 30.09%, the allowance rose from 10.17% to 12.71% of amortized cost, loan losses rose 167.78% and consumer loans 60 days to 89 days past due rose from 2.47% to 4.13%. Losses are provisioned at origination, so growth depresses reported operating income first, and nine-month operating income was 42.49% lower even as gross profit grew; the loan book is therefore both the growth engine and the first place stress would show. Basis: calculation OPINC-9M2026; Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_xyz-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 5, 19–20, 47–48

The unresolved Department of Justice matter is the largest quantified contingent claim on cash: the accrual of USD 764 million equals 48.76% of reported EBITDA and 9.72% of cash, with final terms, court approval and payment timing not stated and losses above the accrual reasonably possible. It is affordable from cash on hand, which is why it is a constraint on the profile and not a threat to liquidity, but it would be less comfortable if paid while repurchases resumed. Basis: calculation DOJ-COVER-20260930; Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_xyz-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 34–35

Control and financial policy are adequate but unproven: a Class B holder group casts 52.41% of the votes, no dividend has ever been declared, repurchases fell from 78.65% to 23.35% of operating cash flow and no notes were issued in the first nine months of 2026, yet the leverage covenant level is not printed and capacity to extract value is unknown without the executed documents. Governance is a medium risk rather than a strength. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_xyz-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 8, 28, 31, 138

Gross profit growth supports deleveraging if it persists: management guides 2026 gross profit to 21.87% above FY2025 and an Adjusted Operating Income margin on gross profit of 27.87%, and nine-month gross margin rose to 48.01% from 41.73% as low-margin bitcoin revenue fell. The guidance is not reconciled to GAAP, so it frames the outlook and does not prove it. Basis: calculation GUIDANCE-2026-2027; calculation GROSSMARGIN-9M2026; EX-99.1_2026-11-03_q32026shareholderletter.htm.jsonl, pages 7–8; 10-Q_2026-09-30_xyz-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 5

runs.text: Liquidity and net cash are the first strength. Cash and cash equivalents exceed all debt including matched warehouse funding, cover the 2027 convertible notes 13.67x and sit beside an undrawn USD 900 million revolver, which means maturities and the regulatory payment can be met from cash without market access in the next 12 months to 24 months. Basis: calculation CASHCOV-20260930; calculation LIQCOV-20260930; Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_xyz-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 27–28, 55

A distant and ladder-like maturity profile is the second strength. The first note maturity is the USD 575 million convertible on November 1, 2027 and the senior notes mature from 2030 to 2033, so refinancing pressure arrives later, which gives time for the regulatory matter to be settled and for the lending cycle to show its credit performance. Basis: calculation WALL-2030-2033; Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_xyz-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 27

Scale and diversification across two ecosystems are the third strength. Two reportable segments, three revenue lines, no customer above 5% of Square payment volume and Square processing revenue that grew in line with payment volume give gross profit a broader base than a single product, which supports cash-flow visibility. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_xyz-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 8; 10-Q_2026-09-30_xyz-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 39, 44

Cash-funded capital policy is the fourth strength. No dividend has ever been declared, the 2026 maturities of USD 1,575 million were repaid from cash and repurchases fell sharply as a share of operating cash flow, so leverage has not been raised to fund shareholder returns. Basis: calculation FCFPROXY-9M2026; calculation REPAY-2026; Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_xyz-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 8, 27

Measure-dependent earnings are the first weakness. Reported EBITDA and adjusted EBITDA differ by add-backs equal to 63.87% of the adjusted figure, and reported operating income fell 42.49% in nine months, so lenders cannot rely on the adjusted measure for debt service capacity. Basis: calculation ADDBACK-LTM; calculation OPINC-9M2026; Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_xyz-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 5, 53–54

Retained consumer lending credit risk is the second weakness. Loans held for investment grew 30.09%, loan losses rose 167.78% and early delinquency rose, so a downturn in consumer credit would reduce operating cash flow and use balance sheet funding at the same time. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_xyz-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 19–20, 47–48

The regulatory payment is the third weakness. An accrual of USD 764 million, equal to 48.76% of reported EBITDA, has no stated payment date, and the deferred charge concerns anti-money-laundering controls that also matter to the bank subsidiary's standing. Basis: calculation DOJ-COVER-20260930; Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_xyz-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 34–35

Concentrated control and discretionary repurchases are the fourth weakness. A Class B holder group casts 52.41% of the votes and the repurchase program has USD 4.6 billion of authorization left, so cash can be redirected to equity holders by a board elected under that control. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_xyz-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 31, 138

Opaque covenant and bank perimeter are the fifth weakness. The leverage covenant level is not printed and the parent must support a bank subsidiary that funds lending with deposits and brokered certificates, so headroom and the claims ranking ahead of note holders cannot be measured. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_xyz-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 91–92; 10-Q_2026-09-30_xyz-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 28, 56

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: No material acquisition, disposal, merger or sponsor transaction is announced or completed in the supplied documents for 2025 or the first nine months of 2026; acquired intangible assets added were USD 5,217 thousand in FY2025 and nothing in the nine months to September 30, 2026. The transactions that matter to creditors are financing, capital-return and settlement events. The documents name Afterpay as an acquisition but state neither its date nor its price, and they describe TIDAL without an acquisition history, although goodwill of USD 73.5 million on the TIDAL reporting unit was impaired in the fourth quarter of 2024. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_xyz-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 6, 78, 180–181; 10-Q_2026-09-30_xyz-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 22

New debt in the last three years: USD 2.0 billion of 6.50% senior unsecured notes due May 15, 2032, issued May 9, 2024, and USD 2.2 billion of senior unsecured notes issued August 18, 2025, of which USD 1.2 billion bear 5.625% and mature August 15, 2030 and USD 1.0 billion bear 6.000% and mature August 15, 2033, with issuance costs of USD 28.3 million. No notes were issued in the nine months to September 30, 2026, and the documents state no use of proceeds for either issue. Each of these series gives holders a repurchase right at 101% on a change of control triggering event, and the indentures, as summarised, restrict liens, certain indebtedness of domestic restricted subsidiaries, sale-leasebacks and transfers of all or substantially all assets. Basis: calculation ISSCOST-20250818; 10-K_2025-12-31_xyz-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 111, 144, 188–190; 10-Q_2026-09-30_xyz-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 27

Capital return: the board raised the repurchase authorization by USD 5 billion to USD 9 billion in November 2025, USD 4.4 billion had been repurchased by September 30, 2026 and USD 4.6 billion remained, with USD 700.9 million bought in the first nine months of 2026 and none in the third quarter. Basis: calculation BBPROG-20260930; 10-K_2025-12-31_xyz-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 111, 203; 10-Q_2026-09-30_xyz-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 31, 143

Other 2026 events: the revolving credit agreement was amended and restated on January 14, 2026 to USD 900 million maturing January 14, 2031 with a springing earlier date, replacing the USD 250.0 million minimum liquidity test with a maximum total net leverage test whose level is not printed; the 2026 convertible notes of USD 575.0 million were repaid on May 1, 2026 and the 2026 senior notes of USD 1.0 billion on June 1, 2026; the warehouse lines now total USD 2.4 billion with USD 1.5 billion drawn; and Square Financial Services began issuing brokered certificates of deposit in the third quarter. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_xyz-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 196–197; 10-Q_2026-09-30_xyz-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 27–29, 56

October 2026 events follow the September 30 balance sheet date and are kept apart from period figures: Block agreed in principle to a three-year deferred prosecution agreement with a gross monetary component of about USD 964 million and a net payment of about USD 764 million, which was accrued at September 30, and agreed in principle a global settlement of the derivative actions that includes USD 150 million from insurers; both remain subject to final agreement and court approval. Basis: calculation DOJ-ACCRUAL; 10-Q_2026-09-30_xyz-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 34–36

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Financial foundation for Block, Inc. (issuer id xyz), as of 2026-11-05, on the credit snapshot pathway. Scope: the audited fiscal 2025 and 2024 statements and the unaudited nine-month 2026 and 2025 statements, normalised on one basis, with debt, cash, liquidity and leverage measures for the latest balance-sheet date.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Source readiness (CP-0), sha256 e2fef1f2e8cd622f6df897a62ac10760012c962b492b10cb3d5cd60b05a9546c: source gate, perimeter and gap list; the covenant level and the executed financing documents are absent.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Block's debt is serviceable, but leverage depends on which earnings measure creditors accept: 4.64x on reported EBITDA against 1.68x on the issuer's adjusted measure for the twelve months to September 30, 2026.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation LEV-2026-09-30; calculation LTM-EBITDA; 10-Q_2026-09-30_xyz-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 27, 50–54

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The gap comes from add-backs the issuer excludes, and contingency and restructuring charges are the largest of them, ahead of share-based compensation, so part of the difference is cash that has left or is still to leave rather than an accounting item.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity is not the constraint: cash exceeds total debt including the matched warehouse funding, which makes net debt negative on the balance sheet, and the revolver is undrawn, but the level of its leverage covenant is not disclosed, so headroom cannot be calculated.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Gross debt, counting every debt line on the balance sheet, fell from USD 8653.901 million at December 31, 2025 to USD 7266.567 million at September 30, 2026, because the 2026 convertible notes and the 2026 senior notes were repaid from cash and no new notes were issued, while warehouse funding rose from USD 1364.883 million to USD 1543.540 million. Cash and cash equivalents rose over the same months, so net debt moved from USD 2089.809 million to USD -592.747 million; the negative figure is net cash. The warehouse debt is matched funding of consumer receivables and loans held by separate entities whose assets are not available to the issuer's other creditors, so the notes alone, USD 5723.027 million at carrying value, are the claim that ranks against the issuer's own resources.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_xyz-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 4–5, 27–30; calculation NETDEBT-2026-09-30; calculation NETDEBT-FY2025

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Leverage is therefore measure-dependent. Reported EBITDA, built as operating income plus depreciation and amortization because the issuer states no unadjusted EBITDA, was USD 1566.955 million for the twelve months to September 30, 2026, against USD 4336.429 million on the issuer's adjusted measure. The difference of USD 2769.474 million is share-based compensation of USD 1038.104 million, contingency, restructuring and other charges of USD 1597.003 million, restructuring share-based compensation of USD 126.639 million and small items. Share-based compensation is a recurring cost the adjusted measure excludes. The charge add-back is described by the issuer as including severance, contingent losses and certain litigation and regulatory charges; the severance reserve was fully paid by September 30, 2026, while the Department of Justice accrual is unpaid, but the filing does not itemise the add-back, so its split is not established. Neither extreme is a clean read: the reported measure is depressed by charges that should not recur, and the adjusted measure is flattered by costs that are real.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation BRIDGE-LTM; calculation LTM-EBITDA; 10-Q_2026-09-30_xyz-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 34–35, 40, 53–54

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Interest cover shows the same split. Cash interest paid for the twelve months was USD 393.057 million against USD 246.331 million in fiscal 2025, because the senior notes issued in August 2025 carry coupons that were first paid in 2026, and cover is 3.99x on reported EBITDA against 11.03x on adjusted EBITDA. Cash interest paid may include interest on warehouse funding, which the issuer books in general and administrative expense, so the ratio is on a broader interest base than the income statement line.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Operating cash flow of USD 3001.581 million for nine months of 2026 is far above net income of USD 342.615 million, because the cash flow statement adds back transaction, loan and consumer receivable losses of USD 1687.281 million and share-based compensation of USD 871.220 million, and shows an inflow of USD 777.910 million from other assets and liabilities that the statement does not break down. Operating cash flow includes the movement in loans originally classified as held for sale and the movement in customers payable, so it is not a clean measure of cash earnings.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Near-term liquidity is ample against dated obligations. No note matures before the 2027 convertible notes on November 1, 2027, the warehouse facilities have USD 447.437 million falling due within a year, and the revolver is undrawn at USD 900.000 million. The claims that could draw on cash are the share repurchase programme, which absorbed USD 700.935 million in nine months, and the Department of Justice resolution accrued at USD 764.000 million with its payment date not stated.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Customers payable, a non-debt funding float, were USD 7700.091 million at September 30, 2026 against USD 6805.366 million at December 31, 2025, an increase of USD 894.725 million, partly matched on the asset side by customer funds of USD 5356.911 million. The issuer excludes customer funds from its liquidity, and this module excludes them from cash, but the obligation is repayable on demand and is the obligation most exposed to a confidence shock. Interest-bearing deposits at the bank subsidiary rose by USD 604.593 million in nine months and brokered deposits began in the third quarter; these fund cash that is counted here, which makes part of the net cash position deposit-funded.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Two events after reporting dates are kept out of period figures. The annual report records, as a subsequent event, the workforce reduction announced on February 26, 2026 with estimated charges of USD 450 million to USD 500 million, and the nine-month report shows USD 495.012 million charged; neither is in fiscal 2025 figures. The agreement in principle with the Department of Justice reached in October 2026 is accrued at September 30, 2026 but not paid, so it is not in any pro forma figure. The revolver restatement of January 14, 2026 and the repayment of the 2026 notes do not change net debt, because debt and cash fall together.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest case against a cautious reading is the balance sheet itself: cash exceeds every debt line, the revolver is undrawn and no note matures before November 2027, so debt service does not depend on either EBITDA measure in the near term. It would win if the Department of Justice payment is met from cash on hand without drawing the revolver and the restructuring charges prove one-off. The strongest case against the benign adjusted reading is the size of the add-backs relative to adjusted EBITDA; it would win if contingency charges recur in later periods or if the unpaid accrual is followed by further regulatory costs, in which case reported leverage and reported cover are the better guide. Part of the cash balance is funded by bank deposits and by customer-related float, so net cash overstates the issuer's own resources.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_xyz-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 28, 34–35, 55–56; calculation LEV-2026-09-30; calculation BRIDGE-LTM

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Borrower, parent, guarantors and a restricted group are not named in any source; the notes and the revolver are described as obligations of the Company. Subsequent events are flagged by date: the workforce reduction plan announced on February 26, 2026 (annual report), the revolver restatement of January 14, 2026, the repayment of the 2026 convertible notes on May 1, 2026 and of the 2026 senior notes on June 1, 2026, and the agreement in principle with the Department of Justice in October 2026 (nine-month report).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Leverage on reported EBITDA is depressed by charges the issuer adds back, and total debt includes matched warehouse funding; the same ratios on adjusted EBITDA are in the calculation register.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cover on adjusted EBITDA is much higher and is shown in the calculation register; the cash interest base may include warehouse interest.

fields.value: The issuer's own liquidity of USD 10,064.035 million at September 30, 2026 also counts restricted cash and marketable securities, which this table leaves out.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Warehouse amounts are shown by final maturity; the facilities are revolving, so drawn balances move with the receivables they fund.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Revenue includes bitcoin ecosystem revenue, which carries almost no margin, and Adjusted EBITDA adds back share-based compensation and charges.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The order within rank 2 follows maturity, not a stated ranking, and the legal rank of the warehouse facilities relative to the unsecured debt is the issuer's security over entity-level assets, not a ranking any source states.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Contingency and restructuring charges and share-based compensation make up nearly all of the add-backs; the bridge states the issuer's own adjustments and does not judge whether they will recur.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Each row works one figure from the inputs shown, in USD thousands or US$m as labelled; the money tables restate thousands in millions without rounding.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The level and definition of the maximum total net leverage ratio in the restated credit agreement are not printed in any source, so covenant headroom is not calculable for any period; this restricts every conclusion about revolver availability; severity High; the action is to obtain the restated credit agreement.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The Department of Justice resolution is an agreement in principle accrued at USD 764.000 million at September 30, 2026 with no final agreement, payment amount, schedule or funding source stated, so no pro forma net debt can be built and the timing of the cash outflow against liquidity is not established; severity High; the action is to update the figures when the agreement is signed.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - No balance sheet at September 30, 2025 is in the sources, so the nine months 2025 column of the balance sheet is not supplied and interim leverage is stated for September 30, 2026 only; severity Medium; the action is to add the third-quarter 2025 report.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Assets by reportable segment are not presented and no stand-alone parent or bank-subsidiary statements are supplied, so corporate cash and debt cannot be separated from bank, customer-funds and warehouse items except through the notes; severity Medium; the action is to request segment assets and parent-only data.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - No borrower scope, guarantor or restricted group is named for the notes, the revolver or the warehouse facilities, so the obligor scope in the debt stack states only the Company and the warehouse special-purpose entities; severity Medium; the action is to obtain the indentures and the credit agreement.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The balance sheet lines the third-quarter report folds into other lines (property and equipment, long-term debt securities, operating lease assets, deferred tax liabilities and operating lease liabilities) are not supplied for September 30, 2026, and short-term investments are not shown separately; severity Low; the action is to use the quarterly balance sheet detail if filed.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Cash flow statement dashes are shown as not supplied rather than zero: proceeds from senior notes in nine months 2026, repayments of senior notes in the earlier columns, convertible note redemptions in FY2024, and the goodwill and intangible impairment add-back in FY2025 and both nine-month periods; the current portion of long-term debt at September 30, 2026 is read as nil because the notes table total equals long-term debt; severity Low; no action beyond the filings.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Discrete quarterly cash flows are not printed, only cumulative figures, so no third-quarter 2026 or 2025 cash flow column is built; a third-quarter column could be derived as nine months less six months from the second-quarter report if discrete quarters are needed; severity Low.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The floor and margin of the revolver and warehouse facilities, the commitment of each warehouse facility (only an aggregate printed as USD 2.4 billion) and the definition of liquidity in the revolver maturity test are not printed; severity Low; the action is to obtain the credit agreement and facility documents.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Whether cash interest paid includes interest on the warehouse facilities is not stated, so interest cover is on an interest base of uncertain breadth; severity Low; the action is to confirm with the issuer.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Reported EBITDA is calculated because the issuer states only Adjusted EBITDA; share-based compensation is not added back, so reported EBITDA is conservative against the issuer's measure; severity Low; the action is none, both measures are shown.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Warehouse availability at December 31, 2024 is not printed, so the FY2024 liquidity row excludes it; severity Low; the action is none.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Business and governance review of Block, Inc. (issuer id xyz), as of 2026-11-05, on the credit snapshot pathway. Scope: business and operating model, ownership and control, transactions, dated history and governance and capital-allocation behaviour, from the seven supplied files and the Source readiness review.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Source readiness (CP-0), sha256 e2fef1f2e8cd622f6df897a62ac10760012c962b492b10cb3d5cd60b05a9546c: source gate, perimeter and gap list; the proxy statement, the executed financing documents and the covenant level are absent.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Block carries medium governance and sponsor risk for creditors: there is no financial sponsor to support them, a Class B holder group casting 52.41% of the votes decides stockholder matters, and protection rests on the issuer's own cash and covenants.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The exposure that matters most is Cash App lending, where loan losses rose 167.78% in nine months, while bitcoin supplies 28.33% of revenue but only 2.07% of gross profit. Creditors hold notes of USD 5,775 million whose indentures, as the issuer summarises the 2030, 2032 and 2033 series, limit liens, certain subsidiary debt, sale-leasebacks and asset transfers, and a USD 764 million regulatory accrual has no stated payment date.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation LOSS-9M2026; calculation REVMIX-9M2026; calculation GPMIX-9M2026; calculation PRINC-20260930; 10-Q_2026-09-30_xyz-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 27, 34; 10-K_2025-12-31_xyz-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 189, 191

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Control sits with a Class B holder group and not with a sponsor, and its vote far exceeds its economic stake: Class B shares are 9.92% of shares outstanding but cast 52.41% of the votes, so Class B holders can approve or block any matter put to stockholders. The issuer names Jack Dorsey as the controlling shareholder for the bank regulator's purposes and says the Class B group includes executive officers, employees and directors, but the proxy statement that would name holders and stakes is not supplied. No equity injection, cure, dividend recapitalisation, sponsor fee or related financing appears in any supplied document, so willingness to support creditors has not been tested either way.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Shareholder returns are large but cash-funded and slowing: repurchases were 23.35% of operating cash flow in the first nine months of 2026 against 78.65% a year earlier, no dividend has ever been declared, and no shares were repurchased in the third quarter, with USD 4.6 billion of the USD 9 billion authorization still available. The program is discretionary and can resume at any time, so it is capacity for cash leakage rather than a commitment, and the credit agreement's customary limits on dividends and repurchases are the only brake the supplied documents describe, at a level not printed.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation BBOCF-9M2026; calculation BBOCF-9M2025; calculation BBPROG-20260930; 10-Q_2026-09-30_xyz-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 8, 31, 43, 143; 10-K_2025-12-31_xyz-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 71, 107

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Gross profit is concentrated in Cash App and in lending-linked products: Cash App supplied 63.92% of nine-month 2026 gross profit and Square 35.43%, and the Financial solutions line, which carries the lending, supplied 41.39% of gross profit against 36.13% a year earlier. Square gives a steadier base, because no customer exceeded 5% of Square payment volume in 2025, 2024 or 2023, but Square gross profit grew 12.11% against 32.11% for Cash App, so the faster-growing franchise also carries most of the retained loan book, 78.22% of loans held for investment at amortized cost.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation SEGGP-9M2026; calculation GPMIX-9M2026; calculation GPMIX-9M2025; calculation SEGGP-GROWTH; calculation LOANMIX-20260930; 10-K_2025-12-31_xyz-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 8; 10-Q_2026-09-30_xyz-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 5, 19, 39

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Retained consumer lending is the exposure most likely to move creditor outcomes. Loans held for investment grew 30.09% in nine months, the allowance rose from 10.17% to 12.71% of amortized cost, and consumer loans 60 days to 89 days past due rose from 2.47% to 4.13% of consumer balances. The issuer says underlying loss rates are stable and the reserve build shows provisioning ahead of growth, but the delinquency movement is the first signal to watch because the retained book sits on the balance sheet and is part-funded by bank deposits, brokered certificates and the warehouse lines.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation LOANS-20260930; calculation DELINQ-20260930; 10-Q_2026-09-30_xyz-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 19–20, 23, 29, 47–48

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Bitcoin inflates revenue without adding to creditor cash flow: it supplied 28.33% of nine-month 2026 revenue and 2.07% of gross profit, against 36.35% and 4.02% a year earlier, so revenue-based scale measures overstate the business and understate the weight of lending. Block also holds a long-term bitcoin investment valued at USD 771.9 million whose fair-value changes run through net income, with a loss of USD 31.6 million in the nine months, which adds earnings volatility that is not operating cash.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation REVMIX-9M2026; calculation REVMIX-9M2025; calculation GPMIX-9M2026; calculation GPMIX-9M2025; 10-Q_2026-09-30_xyz-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 44, 49, 56

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The compliance record is a clear governance weakness. The agreement in principle with the Department of Justice rests on a deferred charge that Block failed to maintain an effective anti-money-laundering program, and the accrual stepped up from USD 240 million at the first quarter to USD 526 million at the second and USD 764 million at the third, against a gross monetary component of about USD 964 million, with final terms, court approval and payment timing still open. The board formed a special litigation committee in April 2026 and the derivative actions reached a settlement in principle that includes USD 150 million from insurers, so a response is visible, but it does not remove the cash call, which equals 7.59% of total liquidity at September 30, 2026.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation DOJ-ACCRUAL; calculation DOJ-LIQ; 10-Q_2026-03-31_xyz-20260331.htm.jsonl, pages 30–31; 10-Q_2026-06-30_xyz-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 32–33; 10-Q_2026-09-30_xyz-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 34–36, 55

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The parent stands behind a regulated bank subsidiary, which adds a claim on parent liquidity. Square Financial Services must hold FDIC capital levels with a leverage ratio of at least 20%, the parent must act as a source of financial strength, and a USD 50 million reserve deposit and a third-party credit line are required; the bank began issuing brokered certificates of deposit in the third quarter, USD 381.4 million at par, all due within twelve months. In structural terms, which is this module's reading and not an issuer statement, bank depositors and certificate holders have first claim on the bank's assets, so growth in bank-funded lending moves value away from holders of the parent's notes.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cost actions are real but management-estimated: the workforce fell by more than 40%, charges of USD 495.0 million fell inside the estimate of USD 450 million to USD 500 million, and annualised savings of USD 800 million to USD 900 million are management's figure, partly reinvested, with no independent measure supplied. The savings have not yet shown in reported operating income, because general and administrative expense rose 70% in nine months on litigation and regulatory accruals.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence against a cautious reading is conduct. Block has never declared a dividend, repaid USD 1,575 million of 2026 maturities in cash without any conversion, issued no new notes in the nine months, kept the USD 900 million revolver undrawn, reports compliance with its financial covenants, and had its Securities and Exchange Commission inquiry closed in March 2026 with no enforcement action recommended. Control by the Class B holders has so far coincided with creditor-neutral or creditor-supportive actions, and the nine-month repurchase pace fell from 78.65% to 23.35% of operating cash flow. The issuer also states ratings of BBB- at Fitch, Ba1 at Moody's and BB+ at S&P for 2025, although no agency document is supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation REPAY-2026; calculation BBOCF-9M2026; calculation BBOCF-9M2025; 10-K_2025-12-31_xyz-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 107; 10-Q_2026-09-30_xyz-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 27–28, 34, 58

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The view would turn adverse on a debt-funded distribution or repurchase while the Department of Justice payment is outstanding, a final settlement above the USD 764 million accrued or with operating restrictions, consumer delinquency moving beyond the 4.13% now reported, a leverage covenant level that leaves little headroom once disclosed, a use of the Class B vote to change the capital structure or related-party dealings, or parent cash committed to the bank subsidiary beyond the USD 50 million reserve. It would improve if the proxy statement showed board-level control of capital allocation that is independent of the Class B holders and if the final settlement matched the accrual.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The 2026 proxy statement is not supplied, so named holders, Class B holdings by holder, director independence, committee membership and executive pay are not established; the control conclusion rests on the issuer's aggregate voting statement and cannot say who would act or how.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The indentures and the restated credit agreement are not supplied, so limits on shareholder payments, investments and new debt are read only from the issuer's summaries; the conclusion on protection against value extraction is a statement of unknown capacity, not of limited capacity.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - No dates, prices or funding for the Afterpay acquisition are supplied and TIDAL has no acquisition history, so the view on acquisition appetite rests on the absence of any material acquisition in 2025 and 2026 and not on a funding history.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Customer and activity counts are management's unaudited measures given only for December 2025 and September 2026, so operating durability is judged on reported direction and not on cohort or retention data.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The Department of Justice resolution is an agreement in principle, so the USD 764 million accrual may change and its effect on liquidity cannot be timed; the governance conclusion on compliance is provisional until the final agreement is signed.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - No market, peer or rating-agency document is supplied, so how lenders price governance and control is not assessed and the stated ratings rest on the issuer's own statement.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: No material acquisition, disposal, merger or sponsor transaction is announced or completed in the supplied documents for 2025 or the first nine months of 2026; acquired intangible assets added were USD 5,217 thousand in FY2025 and nothing in the nine months to September 30, 2026. The transactions that matter to creditors are financing, capital-return and settlement events. The documents name Afterpay as an acquisition but state neither its date nor its price, and they describe TIDAL without an acquisition history, although goodwill of USD 73.5 million on the TIDAL reporting unit was impaired in the fourth quarter of 2024.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: New debt in the last three years: USD 2.0 billion of 6.50% senior unsecured notes due May 15, 2032, issued May 9, 2024, and USD 2.2 billion of senior unsecured notes issued August 18, 2025, of which USD 1.2 billion bear 5.625% and mature August 15, 2030 and USD 1.0 billion bear 6.000% and mature August 15, 2033, with issuance costs of USD 28.3 million. No notes were issued in the nine months to September 30, 2026, and the documents state no use of proceeds for either issue. Each of these series gives holders a repurchase right at 101% on a change of control triggering event, and the indentures, as summarised, restrict liens, certain indebtedness of domestic restricted subsidiaries, sale-leasebacks and transfers of all or substantially all assets.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Capital return: the board raised the repurchase authorization by USD 5 billion to USD 9 billion in November 2025, USD 4.4 billion had been repurchased by September 30, 2026 and USD 4.6 billion remained, with USD 700.9 million bought in the first nine months of 2026 and none in the third quarter.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Other 2026 events: the revolving credit agreement was amended and restated on January 14, 2026 to USD 900 million maturing January 14, 2031 with a springing earlier date, replacing the USD 250.0 million minimum liquidity test with a maximum total net leverage test whose level is not printed; the 2026 convertible notes of USD 575.0 million were repaid on May 1, 2026 and the 2026 senior notes of USD 1.0 billion on June 1, 2026; the warehouse lines now total USD 2.4 billion with USD 1.5 billion drawn; and Square Financial Services began issuing brokered certificates of deposit in the third quarter.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: October 2026 events follow the September 30 balance sheet date and are kept apart from period figures: Block agreed in principle to a three-year deferred prosecution agreement with a gross monetary component of about USD 964 million and a net payment of about USD 764 million, which was accrued at September 30, and agreed in principle a global settlement of the derivative actions that includes USD 150 million from insurers; both remain subject to final agreement and court approval.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Module status: Ready with Limitations, because the ownership, director and pay documents and the executed financing documents are not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The risk level is driven by Class B voting control, a large discretionary repurchase program and an unresolved compliance matter, because together they let cash leave or be committed outside creditor control, which implies a moderate chance of weaker liquidity cover and no evidenced support for creditors. Countervailing evidence is the absence of any dividend, sponsor fee, liability-management transaction or debt-funded distribution in the supplied documents, and repayment of maturities from cash.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Overall, Block presents medium sponsor and governance risk. The key supported behaviour is cash-funded repurchases under Class B voting control, which matters because cash can leave outside creditor control and implies a sensitivity to the Department of Justice payment. Countervailing evidence is that no dividend, sponsor fee, liability-management transaction or debt-funded distribution is documented. Further analysis requires the proxy statement, the executed financing documents and the final agreement with the Department of Justice.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Governance review completed with limitations. Sponsor / Governance Risk Level: Medium. Key gaps: proxy statement, executed financing documents and final Department of Justice terms.

The primary downside path is a credit-loss and regulatory cash squeeze on a lending book that the parent carries on its own balance sheet.

fields.value: Liquidity is the strongest support and does most of the work: cash and cash equivalents cover the 2027 convertible notes 13.67x, issuer-stated total liquidity covers the notes principal 1.74x, the USD 900 million revolver is undrawn, no senior note falls due before 2030, and 90.04% of the notes principal falls due in four series from 2030 to 2033. Part of the cash is deposit-funded and customer-related float is large, so the cushion is real but not all of it is the issuer's own money.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation CASHCOV-20260930; calculation LIQCOV-20260930; calculation WALL-2030-2033; Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_xyz-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 4, 27–28, 55–56

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Leverage is measure-dependent, so no single ratio settles the credit: total debt is 4.64x reported EBITDA and 1.68x adjusted EBITDA, notes alone are 3.65x and 1.32x, and interest cover is 3.99x reported against 11.03x adjusted. The add-backs are 63.87% of adjusted EBITDA and include the contingency and restructuring charges that are partly cash, so the reported figures are the safer guide until the regulatory matter is settled.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation NOTESLEV-20260930; calculation ADDBACK-LTM; Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_xyz-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 53–54

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cash flow is strong but not clean: operating cash flow in nine months of 2026 was 53.24% higher than a year earlier and purchases of property and equipment were only 4.26% of it, leaving a proxy of USD 2,873,585 thousand, yet the figure includes movements in loans and customer balances and an unexplained inflow in other assets and liabilities. Light capital intensity gives flexibility, but conversion of earnings to free cash is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation FCFPROXY-9M2026; Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_xyz-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 7–8

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Retained consumer lending is the main credit-quality exposure: loans held for investment grew 30.09%, the allowance rose from 10.17% to 12.71% of amortized cost, loan losses rose 167.78% and consumer loans 60 days to 89 days past due rose from 2.47% to 4.13%. Losses are provisioned at origination, so growth depresses reported operating income first, and nine-month operating income was 42.49% lower even as gross profit grew; the loan book is therefore both the growth engine and the first place stress would show.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation OPINC-9M2026; Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_xyz-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 5, 19–20, 47–48

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The unresolved Department of Justice matter is the largest quantified contingent claim on cash: the accrual of USD 764 million equals 48.76% of reported EBITDA and 9.72% of cash, with final terms, court approval and payment timing not stated and losses above the accrual reasonably possible. It is affordable from cash on hand, which is why it is a constraint on the profile and not a threat to liquidity, but it would be less comfortable if paid while repurchases resumed.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation DOJ-COVER-20260930; Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_xyz-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 34–35

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Control and financial policy are adequate but unproven: a Class B holder group casts 52.41% of the votes, no dividend has ever been declared, repurchases fell from 78.65% to 23.35% of operating cash flow and no notes were issued in the first nine months of 2026, yet the leverage covenant level is not printed and capacity to extract value is unknown without the executed documents. Governance is a medium risk rather than a strength.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Gross profit growth supports deleveraging if it persists: management guides 2026 gross profit to 21.87% above FY2025 and an Adjusted Operating Income margin on gross profit of 27.87%, and nine-month gross margin rose to 48.01% from 41.73% as low-margin bitcoin revenue fell. The guidance is not reconciled to GAAP, so it frames the outlook and does not prove it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation GUIDANCE-2026-2027; calculation GROSSMARGIN-9M2026; EX-99.1_2026-11-03_q32026shareholderletter.htm.jsonl, pages 7–8; 10-Q_2026-09-30_xyz-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 5

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence for a stronger view is the balance sheet: cash exceeds every debt line, net cash equals 0.38x reported EBITDA, no note falls due before November 2027 and the issuer states an investment-grade rating from Fitch of BBB-. The strongest evidence for a weaker view is the pace of retained lending, where loan losses rose 167.78% in nine months while nine-month operating income fell 42.49%, and an unresolved payment equal to 48.76% of reported EBITDA. The adequate view holds because liquidity absorbs the payment and the lending growth is, on the issuer's account, matched by stable loss rates.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_xyz-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 28, 34–35, 47–48, 58

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The view would move up if the final settlement matched the accrual and was paid from cash, the executed credit agreement showed ample headroom under the net leverage test, and delinquency stopped rising. It would move down if consumer loans 60 days to 89 days past due kept rising beyond 4.13%, if the final settlement exceeded the accrual or brought operating conditions, if repurchases resumed at the pace of 2025, or if bank funding or warehouse availability tightened while originations kept growing.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation DOJ-COVER-20260930; Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_xyz-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 20, 29–30, 34–35, 56

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The level and definition of the maximum total net leverage covenant are not printed, so headroom, and with it the reliability of the revolver as a backstop in a stress, cannot be assessed; the liquidity conclusion assumes the facility stays available.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Reported EBITDA is built from operating income and depreciation because the issuer states only adjusted EBITDA, so every leverage and cover conclusion carries a range between the two measures and not a single reading.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - No peer figures, traded prices or agency reports are supplied, so the view that the profile is adequate is absolute and not relative, and market access is judged from a 2025 issue and the issuer's own ratings statement.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - No stand-alone parent or bank subsidiary statements are supplied, so the split of cash and funding between the corporate group, the bank and customer-related float rests on notes, and the net cash conclusion could be overstated by deposit-funded cash.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Loss history by origination cohort is not supplied for consumer lending, so the conclusion on credit quality rests on reserve ratios and delinquency movements over two dates and cannot separate growth effects from deterioration.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Management guidance is non-GAAP and carries no cash flow, capital spending or debt service guidance, so the outlook conclusions describe earnings direction only and give no forward view of free cash flow.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity and net cash are the first strength. Cash and cash equivalents exceed all debt including matched warehouse funding, cover the 2027 convertible notes 13.67x and sit beside an undrawn USD 900 million revolver, which means maturities and the regulatory payment can be met from cash without market access in the next 12 months to 24 months.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation CASHCOV-20260930; calculation LIQCOV-20260930; Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_xyz-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 27–28, 55

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: A distant and ladder-like maturity profile is the second strength. The first note maturity is the USD 575 million convertible on November 1, 2027 and the senior notes mature from 2030 to 2033, so refinancing pressure arrives later, which gives time for the regulatory matter to be settled and for the lending cycle to show its credit performance.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation WALL-2030-2033; Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_xyz-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 27

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Scale and diversification across two ecosystems are the third strength. Two reportable segments, three revenue lines, no customer above 5% of Square payment volume and Square processing revenue that grew in line with payment volume give gross profit a broader base than a single product, which supports cash-flow visibility.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cash-funded capital policy is the fourth strength. No dividend has ever been declared, the 2026 maturities of USD 1,575 million were repaid from cash and repurchases fell sharply as a share of operating cash flow, so leverage has not been raised to fund shareholder returns.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation FCFPROXY-9M2026; calculation REPAY-2026; Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_xyz-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 8, 27

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Measure-dependent earnings are the first weakness. Reported EBITDA and adjusted EBITDA differ by add-backs equal to 63.87% of the adjusted figure, and reported operating income fell 42.49% in nine months, so lenders cannot rely on the adjusted measure for debt service capacity.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation ADDBACK-LTM; calculation OPINC-9M2026; Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_xyz-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 5, 53–54

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Retained consumer lending credit risk is the second weakness. Loans held for investment grew 30.09%, loan losses rose 167.78% and early delinquency rose, so a downturn in consumer credit would reduce operating cash flow and use balance sheet funding at the same time.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The regulatory payment is the third weakness. An accrual of USD 764 million, equal to 48.76% of reported EBITDA, has no stated payment date, and the deferred charge concerns anti-money-laundering controls that also matter to the bank subsidiary's standing.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation DOJ-COVER-20260930; Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_xyz-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 34–35

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Concentrated control and discretionary repurchases are the fourth weakness. A Class B holder group casts 52.41% of the votes and the repurchase program has USD 4.6 billion of authorization left, so cash can be redirected to equity holders by a board elected under that control.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Opaque covenant and bank perimeter are the fifth weakness. The leverage covenant level is not printed and the parent must support a bank subsidiary that funds lending with deposits and brokered certificates, so headroom and the claims ranking ahead of note holders cannot be measured.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_xyz-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 91–92; 10-Q_2026-09-30_xyz-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 28, 56

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Block runs two connected ecosystems, Square for sellers and Cash App for consumers, with TIDAL and bitcoin hardware projects outside the two reportable segments, and reports revenue as Commerce enablement, Financial solutions and Bitcoin ecosystem. Gross profit is the measure management steers by, because bitcoin revenue is the price of bitcoin sold to customers and carries almost no margin. Gross profit was USD 10,359,929 thousand in FY2025 and was 24.35% higher in nine months of 2026 than a year earlier, and the base is broad: no customer exceeded 5% of Square payment volume, the United States is 91.00% of revenue and the operating record runs from 2009.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The credit linkage is that processing and software income follows seller volume and gives visibility, lending income is repeat but short-dated and loss-bearing, and licences across payments, banking, lending, brokerage and bitcoin mean a regulatory action can restrict products that earn gross profit. Seasonality exists but is not quantified in the documents, with Square strongest in the fourth quarter and Cash App lifted by tax refunds in the first. Afterpay is the only acquisition the documents name, and its date and price are not stated.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Block is a listed company with no financial sponsor and concentrated voting control: a Class B holder group casts 52.41% of the votes with 9.92% of the shares, and Jack Dorsey is named as controlling shareholder for the bank regulator's purposes. The issuer of the senior notes and the convertible notes is the parent, no guarantor is named, and the debt that ranks ahead structurally sits in two places, the matched warehouse entities whose assets are not available to the parent's creditors and the bank subsidiary whose deposits and certificates rank first on its assets.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Leverage tolerance is low on the evidence, with net cash, no dividends, maturities repaid from cash and no new notes in 2026, but capacity to take on debt or pay shareholders cannot be read without the executed documents. Governance is a medium risk because control is concentrated, the compliance record led to a deferred charge and the proxy statement that would show board independence is not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Revenue is driven by volume and by lending volume, not by price. Square processing grew in line with payment volume, Commerce enablement revenue grew with Cash App Card and Afterpay Post-Purchase, and Financial solutions revenue grew 40.26% in nine months on Cash App Borrow, so growth is real but is increasingly lending-linked. Square sellers sign no mandatory long-term contracts, which keeps pricing transparent and lock-in low, and Cash App acquires customers through free peer-to-peer transfers, so retention rests on product use and not on contract.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The credit implication is that revenue is recurring in behaviour but transactional in form, sensitive to consumer spending and credit conditions and to regulation, and bitcoin revenue, 28.33% of revenue, swings with the bitcoin price without moving gross profit much. Customer concentration is low at Square and not stated for Cash App.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Gross margin rose to 48.01% in nine months of 2026 from 41.73% because low-margin bitcoin revenue fell and higher-margin financial solutions grew, yet operating income was only 7.55% of gross profit against 16.33% a year earlier, because general and administrative expense included an increase of USD 969.2 million in litigation and regulatory accruals, a figure the Business & governance review states without saying it is the nine-month increase and not the level, and loan losses are booked at origination. Costs are part variable, with processing cost following volume and provisions following originations, and part fixed, with cloud purchase commitments of USD 2,201,264 thousand and a workforce that was cut by more than 40%.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Margins can be defended against volume pressure through the cost actions, but not against a rise in loss rates, which would hit operating income before gross profit; margin stability is therefore average and depends on credit performance.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation GROSSMARGIN-9M2026; calculation OPMARGIN-9M2026; 10-Q_2026-09-30_xyz-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 5, 37, 45–47

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Capital intensity is low: purchases of property and equipment were USD 127,996 thousand in nine months of 2026, 4.26% of operating cash flow, and cash paid for interest was USD 270,946 thousand against USD 124,220 thousand a year earlier as the 2025 notes began paying coupons. Operating cash flow of USD 3,001,581 thousand benefits from add-backs of loan losses and share-based compensation and from movements in loans and customers payable, and cash taxes of USD 194,555 thousand and the accrued regulatory payment are still to be absorbed.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Free cash flow after capital spending is a proxy only; the credit implication is that cash interest, at 9.03% of operating cash flow, is comfortably covered in the period but the quality of conversion is not established, and a cash cost of USD 764 million would absorb 26.59% of the nine-month proxy.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation FCFPROXY-9M2026; calculation INTEREST-OCF; Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_xyz-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 7–8, 34, 40

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Rivalry is intense in both ecosystems, from business software providers, acquirers and banks for sellers and from money transfer apps, card issuers, brokerages and banks for consumers, and Block competes on brand, breadth and simplicity, which is not a contractual moat. The threat of new entrants is high in payments and lending because licences and data are available to well-funded fintechs, though Block's seller network and Cash App peer-to-peer network create switching effort. Substitutes include bank transfers, cards and cash, and bitcoin payment rails that Block itself promotes. Buyers have power because sellers sign no long-term contracts, and suppliers have moderate power through card networks, acquiring processors, bank partners and cloud providers whose terms set processing cost and a fixed commitment of USD 2,201,264 thousand.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: For creditors the forces matter through margin: rivalry limits pricing power on processing, so earnings growth must come from volume and lending, which returns the credit to loss performance.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Regulatory and economic factors are material and social and technological ones are secondary. The deferred anti-money-laundering charge, bank-regulator conditions on Square Financial Services and state and federal lending and money transmission licences make regulation a direct driver of cash and permitted products, and consumer credit conditions and the bitcoin price drive loan losses and revenue. Artificial intelligence is credited by management for lower cost and faster product release, but its effect on credit is only the cost savings already estimated.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strengths that support credit are liquidity that exceeds all debt, maturities that begin in November 2027 and then in 2030, a broad seller base without concentration, a workforce cut by more than 40% and no dividend. Weaknesses that constrain credit are the gap between reported and adjusted earnings, retained consumer loans growing faster than the rest of the business, an unresolved payment of USD 764 million and concentrated voting control. Opportunities that could improve credit are gross profit growth guided at 21.87% above FY2025 for 2026, distribution expansion in Square and a final settlement at or below the accrual. Threats that could weaken credit are a consumer credit downturn, bank funding or warehouse availability tightening, regulatory conditions that limit lending, and a bitcoin price fall that cuts revenue and the USD 771.9 million investment.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation GUIDANCE-2026-2027; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); EX-99.1_2026-11-03_q32026shareholderletter.htm.jsonl, pages 7–9; 10-Q_2026-09-30_xyz-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 34, 56

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Ratings-style lens on the nine dimensions, with the metrics carried from the Financial foundation below.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Scale and market position is Strong: FY2025 gross profit was USD 10,359,929 thousand, Square processed USD 250 billion of volume and Cash App reached 60 million monthly transacting actives. Competitive advantage is Average: network effects and an integrated ecosystem are management claims without market share data. Business diversification is Average: two ecosystems and three revenue lines are offset by 63.92% of gross profit from Cash App and 41.39% from Financial solutions. Cost and capex flexibility is Strong: capital spending is 4.26% of operating cash flow and the workforce was cut by more than 40%. Margin stability is Average: gross margin rose to 48.01% while operating income fell 42.49%. Free cash flow stability is Average: strong in the period but not clean and facing a payment of USD 764 million. Ability to refinance and access capital markets is Average: USD 2.2 billion of notes were sold in August 2025 at coupons of 5.625% and 6.000% and ratings are BBB-, Ba1 and BB+, but the covenant level and market data are not supplied. Liquidity position is Strong: USD 10.1 billion of issuer-stated liquidity and net cash. Financial policy and governance is Average: no dividend and cash-funded repurchases against concentrated control and a compliance finding.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Main supports are liquidity and distant maturities; constraints are earnings quality, lending growth and the regulatory payment; the trend is mixed, with total debt to reported EBITDA moving from 4.16x at FY2025 to 4.64x because earnings were depressed by charges, while net debt moved from USD 2,089,809 thousand at FY2025 to net cash of USD 592,747 thousand; key missing data are the covenant level, loss history by cohort and the final regulatory terms.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_xyz-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 8; EX-99.1_2026-11-03_q32026shareholderletter.htm.jsonl, pages 1, 9; 10-Q_2026-09-30_xyz-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 5, 55–56, 58

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Over the next 12 months to 24 months management guides 2026 gross profit to 21.87% above FY2025 and at least 15% growth in 2027 with Adjusted Operating Income margin on gross profit of 27.87% rising to 31.51%, tailwinds being Square distribution, Cash App actives and lending growth and cost savings of USD 800 million to USD 900 million a year; headwinds are the regulatory payment, higher loss provisions as lending grows, cash interest on the 2025 notes and the 2027 convertible maturity on November 1, 2027. In the medium term the senior notes, 90.04% of principal, mature in four series from 2030 to 2033, so refinancing depends on sustained earnings and on lender appetite for a business whose lending share is rising.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Sector tailwinds are digital payments adoption and consumer demand for instant credit; sector headwinds are consumer credit cycles, regulation of small-dollar lending and bitcoin price swings, none of which can be quantified from the documents.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation GUIDANCE-2026-2027; calculation WALL-2030-2033; EX-99.1_2026-11-03_q32026shareholderletter.htm.jsonl, page 7; 10-Q_2026-09-30_xyz-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 27, 34, 43

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The issuer-specific downside begins with consumer credit weakening at Cash App, shown first as 60 days to 89 days past due rising beyond 4.13% and a rising allowance. The first operational break is provisioning: losses are booked at origination, so operating income falls before gross profit does, and Cash App Borrow originations may be curtailed if warehouse, deposit or brokered funding tightens or a regulator conditions the bank. The financial transmission is lower operating cash flow while the Department of Justice payment of about USD 764 million, taxes and any repurchases still draw cash, and reported leverage rises above 4.64x as reported EBITDA falls.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity consequences stay manageable in the period: cash covers the 2027 convertible 13.67x, the revolver is undrawn and no senior note is due before 2030, so resilience appears sufficient to avoid liquidity distress over the next 12 months to 24 months; the exposures are a covenant breach that cannot be tested without the level, and a loss of bank funding that would force the parent to support the bank. Management levers are suspending repurchases, which were already nil in the third quarter, slowing originations and drawing the revolver. Observable triggers are delinquency, the allowance ratio, the final settlement terms and bank capital ratios.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation CASHCOV-20260930; calculation DOJ-COVER-20260930; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_xyz-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 19–20, 28, 34, 56

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Overall, Block presents an adequate business profile supported by two diversified ecosystems, low customer concentration and a workforce that has been cut by more than 40%, but credit quality is constrained by retained consumer lending that is growing fast, a gap between reported and adjusted earnings and an unresolved regulatory payment. Cash-flow durability appears adequate because capital spending is light and operating cash flow is strong, though its quality is not established. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on loss performance, the final settlement and the covenant level, since no note matures until November 2027 and the first senior notes mature in 2030. The primary downside path is credit losses and a regulatory cash call squeezing earnings while the parent carries the lending book and supports the bank. Further analysis would require the executed credit agreement and indentures, loss history by cohort, stand-alone bank statements and the final settlement.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Fundamental credit review completed with limitations. Top risk: retained consumer lending losses combined with the regulatory payment.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_xyz-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 19–20, 28, 34

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Module status: Ready with Limitations, because the covenant level, the executed financing documents, the proxy statement and the final regulatory terms are not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Each row works one figure from the inputs shown, in USD thousand unless stated; the upstream figures it uses are stated in the Financial foundation and no printed amount is adjusted.
